title: Taking the Backward Step
speaker: Kanho Chris Burkhart
summary: Kanho Chris Burkhart opens by reading Mary Oliver's poem "Have You Ever Tried to Enter the Long Black Branches," then takes up Dogen's instruction to "learn the backward step that turns your light inwardly to illuminate yourself." Kanho admits to reading the line many times without understanding it, until one evening it opened. Kanho describes the "forward step" of chasing outcomes, reacting from habit, and seeing separation everywhere, and sets it beside the Genjokoan image of a boat on an ocean that only looks circular. Zazen becomes the backward step, with practice and enlightenment as one word and the map never the territory. A closing poem, "Peaceful Life," ends on practicing right here, now, as living in vows.
